items.title: Manny Gabriel Interview, 1965-07-27
items.q: He played in the band, Joe, played in the band with my daddy, too, Wooden Joe, trumpet, my daddy and Willie Phillip.

ctx.x: You're a buddy of the peace band, huh?

Yeah, it was around the corner of the hoist band with Louis Deming. So, I said, now I'm going to get a saxophone. So, Joe heard about us. Joe said, Joe said, came to the house. He said, man, do you want a saxophone? I heard. I said, yeah, but I ain't got the money to buy nothing. He said, you come up to the house tomorrow and bring any kind of money you want to bring. I'll get your saxophone if you worry about that. So, I went up there and the boy Larry, Larry, he had a saxophone because he must have failed on…
I know Billy Goodson was her name, I guess. From Pensacola. Sadie? What was the name? I don't know. That's Ken. Didi. Didi's wife.

items.title: Manny Gabriel Interview, 1965-07-27
items.q: Joe Oliver, when we would be rehearsing, he would come and rehearsing with my dad. He couldn't leave a number. King Oliver.

ctx.x: See, that's when Louis Armstrong went there.

And the last thing Louis played was a dance for my daddy at the Coliseum. I advertised, not the dance. He played the advertised. I played the clarinet. He left that same night in 1923. First time a dance was ever gave down there. But Sidney Dazman, he played the job. And I played with Sidney Dazman's band, two drums. He just came into me and I played the drum in the band. When I was playing the drum in the band, I was on the drum. Vic was on the tramo, Vic Gasper. And Sidney Dazman on the trumpet. The crew on the…
I know he had the one bad eye.
